_meta.title: Proposed canonical-entity/relationship candidates for the long-tail opportunity-organizer strings (batch 2)
_meta.scope_note: Covers the 147 organizer strings from opportunities.organization NOT already covered by data/research/canonical-entities/opportunity-organizer-candidates.json (the Penn/Wharton cluster, the MIT cluster, and METU/Arber Kongre). Every organizer_string_raw below was cross-checked against a live read-only query of oryn-qa-scratch.opportunities (organization, official_url) on 2026-08-21 -- the official_url already recorded per-opportunity by an earlier researcher was used as a corroborating source alongside independent web research (ROR API for universities/research institutions, each organization's own site for everything else), not as the sole source.
_meta.status: RESEARCH CANDIDATE ONLY -- not written to canonical_entities. For the session that owns write access to review before creating any row, alias, or relationship.
_meta.method: Universities and independent research institutes were looked up against the ROR API (api.ror.org) directly. Every other organizer was researched via each organization's own official website, cross-referenced against the live opportunities.official_url field for the same organizer string where available. Wikipedia/Wikidata were used only as a discovery index, never cited as the source of a value, per this package's standing source-authority rule (RULE-ENTITY-017).
_meta.entity_type_note: opportunities.organization_entity_id's own trigger (migration 0038, trg_opportunities_org_entity_type) only permits entity_type in ('opportunity_provider','organization','university','school','employer','research_institution','lab','ngo','club') -- NOT 'program','competition','scholarship', even though several organizer strings are, in the general 14-type taxonomy, arguably a program/competition by name. Where an organizer string IS the name of a competition/journal/scholarship AND that name is also the organization's own legal/operating identity (no separately-named parent body exists), this batch proposes entity_type='opportunity_provider' -- an organization whose entire public identity is providing that one program -- rather than 'competition'/'program', so the proposal is actually usable against this column. See doc 13 for the full boundary rule between 'opportunity_provider' and generic 'organization' used in this batch.
